overview.short: Sat Deul is a rare 10th–11th century Jain Rekha Deul brick temple located at Deula near Masagram in Purba Bardhaman, West Bengal, rising over 60 feet amidst lush rural countryside.
overview.description: Sat Deul (সাত দেউল) is a protected monumental 10th-century brick temple situated in Deula village in the Memari I region of Purba Bardhaman district, West Bengal. Standing at approximately 60 feet, this curvilinear tower (rekha deul) represents the pinnacle of early medieval Pala-Sena period architectural mastery, adorned with ornate horizontal tiers, chaitya gavaksha arches, and exquisite terracotta floral reliefs in the heart of rural Bengal.
overview.about: Sat Deul is a magnificent 10th-century Jain brick temple in Purba Bardhaman, West Bengal, celebrated for its soaring curvilinear rekha deul shikhara and ancient terracotta artistry.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Sat Deul?
faq.a: The best time to visit Sat Deul is Oct – Mar. Summers are 26–40°C and winters are 12–28°C.

faq.q: How do I reach Sat Deul?
faq.a: The nearest airport is Sat Deul / nearest airport (30 km) and the nearest railway station is Howrah Junction (Kolkata) (70 km). Roads are generally good; check seasonal/monsoon conditions before high-altitude or remote stretches.

faq.q: How many days are enough for Sat Deul?
